How Insight Led to Gratitude

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (895 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As I celebrate Thanksgiving in 2026, I find countless things to be thankful for.
  • Industry observers note that the word “insight” can describe the recognition of a medical condition by the person who has the condition, particularly with a brain disorder like schizophrenia or bipolar disorder.
  • In a recent development, today, living in recovery, I am not just thankful for the positive things in my life.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Lybi Ma.

As I celebrate Thanksgiving in 2026, I find countless things to be thankful for. I have parents and friends, a great church, my college education, my work, and a spacious apartment near my alma mater, the University of Cincinnati. Everything I give thanks for in my life today was made possible by finding an effective antipsychotic medication that enabled me to develop insight into my schizophrenia in 2008. I have lived in full remission from schizophrenia ever since.

Industry observers note that the word “insight” can describe the recognition of a medical condition by the person who has the condition, particularly with a brain disorder like schizophrenia or bipolar disorder. The technical term for a lack of insight into a medical condition is “anosognosia.” Right hemispheric stroke patients often struggle with anosognosia. They may have a paralyzed limb, but when the doctor asks them to move their limb, they come up with excuses such as that they don’t feel like moving their limb at that time, entirely unaware they are paralyzed. Most people with schizophrenia suffer from anosognosia, at least at first. It is a hallmark of schizophrenia. This was my situation beginning in 2006, over a year before I was diagnosed with schizophrenia and began treatment.

In a recent development, today, living in recovery, I am not just thankful for the positive things in my life. I am also deeply grateful for the most basic needs. A shower, a refrigerator, the safety of sleeping in a bed indoors, enough money to go out to eat when I like. For four years, while homeless due to untreated schizophrenia, these were things I didn’t have.

What isolation and estrangement do to a person.

Another thing I did not have when I was homeless due to untreated schizophrenia was family and friends involved in my life. Looking back, I was not aware that my isolation and estrangement from family were entirely due to my own paranoia. My parents had always supported me with kindness, love, and generosity. Today I am deeply grateful to have my parents in my life again and see them often.

Industry observers note that on March 3, 2007, my homelessness ended. That was the day when neighbors called the police on me for screaming back at the voices in my mind, and I was taken to a psychiatric hospital. I hated being in the hospital, but my medication made a huge difference. It eliminated my delusions, paranoia, and most of my hallucinations, and it also left me questioning why I had chosen to become homeless for four years.

Today, I live with healthy insight, aware that I have schizophrenia, which is in full remission on clozapine, and I know that my symptoms of schizophrenia would rapidly return if I were to ever go off my antipsychotic, even for a few days. I also recognize that if I were to go off my clozapine, relapse, and then need to go back on it, it would likely not be nearly as effective as it is today. Unfortunately, many people don't see the danger of inconsistent medication compliance. During the last nearly two decades, I have not missed my clozapine doses. I am thankful that I have developed a level of insight that keeps me stable and healthy.

The connection between insight and thankfulness.

Looking back, I needed insight to perceive reality clearly enough to be thankful.

According to recent reports, I never take my apartment for granted, especially when it rains. I remember sleeping outside under a church overhang, getting soaked, with nowhere else to go.

According to recent reports, today, my refrigerator is filled with healthy food, including vegetables, lots of fresh fruit, and cooking supplies. I will never forget living without knowing where my next meal would come from, and worrying that the food I found would be contaminated and make me sick. I still remember accidently ingesting some metal chips on donuts I found near a construction site, which gave me continual abdominal pain for months.

Recent findings suggest that before I became homeless, I traveled to both Africa and Southeast Asia, but I didn’t bring enough money with me. I remember sleeping in the airport in Hong Kong during an 18-hour layover with no money for a hotel room. I also traveled to both places on my own and took risks, such as living in a slum area of Nairobi, which was highly dangerous for foreigners. During my illness, I felt no sense of danger, due to impaired insight. Today, I am grateful for a clear mind that helps me make smart decisions about my safety.

I am also grateful that I had the opportunity to return to the university and finish my degree, though my first doctors thought that would be highly unlikely.

Perhaps I am most grateful I learned from these horrible things and now give back to society. I have published two books which I use to encourage others and educate families about the experience of schizophrenia. Mind Estranged is a memoir on my illness and recovery, and Awakenings tells the stories of 28 people who, like me, are thriving despite schizophrenia.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Max Verstappen started on pole for the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday evening and held the lead at one point on every lap, but the race was far more thrilling than that would let on.

Verstappen qualified second and inherited pole after pole-sitter Kimi Antonelli received a five-place grid penalty.

At the start, Max Verstappen took the lead from George Russell and kept his elbows out as he had the hardest spot on the track, punching through the crisp air with no help from a slipstream.

Industry observers note that on the second lap of the race, Russell, in a much faster Mercedes, passed Verstappen in the final corners coming off the Las Vegas Strip straight, then lost the lead before the first corner of the next lap. He would repeat this multiple times throughout the first half of the Grand Prix.

The race recorded a record 35 lead changes, but no one could cement a run past Verstappen.

With Verstappen slowing the field behind him, the first 10 laps of the race found the top three within one second and the top ten within less than 4.5 seconds.

Sources indicate that on lap 20, Sergio Perez tried to make a pick on Rafeal Camera and the Haas, and Cadillac ended up tangled in the barrier, bringing out a full safety car. In a normal race, this would’ve neutralized the race, but with everyone still running bunched up, it just sent the field all together to the pits, leading to teams double-stacking against each other.

Hamilton was the biggest loser at the pit stop, having to serve a 10-second penalty that was not yet shared with him for a battle with Norris that he thought was just.

Hamilton was kept out while everyone else pitted to clear space for Charles Leclerc and was told about his penalty.

“Ah, that’s shit. If I turned in, we would’ve crashed.”.

Under the safety car, Arvid Lindblad spun on cold tires to end his campaign for his first-ever podium. Arvid had his best starting spot of fifth for the Grand Prix and ran as high as third, while the Red Bulls on his sister team ran 1-2; he fell out of the points with the mistake.

It has been revealed that shortly after racing resumed, Isack Hadjar, who challenged his teammate Verstappen for the lead in the first half of the race and often put in the hardest position between the leader and the charging field, hit debris on the track and damaged his front wing. Hadjar pitted and finished outside the points as well.

With Red Bull and VCARB drivers out of contention, the door reopened for the Mercedes as Kimi Antonelli made his way into the picture following his grid drop, and Russell never left.

With two laps to go, Antonelli led Russell as the teammate fought for second; in turn 5, Russell went for the pass, overcommitted, and slid into the barrier.

Verstappen laughed on from ahead following a weekend of tension between the front-row starters.

Antonelli fell away from the lead battle on the penultimate lap with an internal glitch and would come home fourth.

In the mayhem, the McLarens saw their luck change at Las Vegas. Following this double disqualification while battling for the championship last year, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri walked away with a shocking first double podium of the season.

“I led for about 15 seconds, so I’m very proud,” Norris joked.

Antonelli was followed by Pierre Gasly, Franco Colapinto, Lewis Hamilton, Carlos Sainz, George Russell and Charles Leclerc in the points-paying positions.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A retired EV battery can still have years of use left in it when it’s taken off the road.
  • Nova was unveiled at RE+ in Las Vegas this week, and it’s already in production at Megafactory 1, the battery-repurposing plant that Moment Energy opened in the Vancouver area in June.
  • In a recent development, each Nova unit delivers 500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy and 200 kilowatts (kW) of power.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A retired EV battery can still have years of use left in it when it’s taken off the road. Moment Energy’s fresh Nova battery storage system puts those packs to work on commercial sites. And when a pack wears out, it can be swapped without pulling out the whole system.

Nova was unveiled at RE+ in Las Vegas this week, and it’s already in production at Megafactory 1, the battery-repurposing plant that Moment Energy opened in the Vancouver area in June.

In a recent development, each Nova unit delivers 500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy and 200 kilowatts (kW) of power. It has a 2.94 m by 1.80 m (9.7 x 5.9 ft) footprint, and units can be linked together for projects in the tens of megawatt-hours. A site could charge the batteries when electricity is cheaper or when its solar panels are producing more than it needs, then draw on that power when demand spikes or the grid goes down.

Nova can use packs from different EV models, even when those packs have aged at different rates. Moment’s battery management software tracks how each pack is doing. As packs wear out, the company can replace them while leaving the enclosure and concrete pad in place. Moment indicates its pack replacement service could keep a system in service for more than 20 years.

In a recent development, “We see a future where reengineered EV batteries become essential infrastructure for powering businesses and onshoring manufacturing and supply chains. Nova brings that vision to life, combining safety, engineering, and North American manufacturing to deploy the safest and highest-performance batteries ever made: EV batteries to supercharge our aging grid,” noted Edward Chiang, co-founder and CEO of Moment Energy.

Moment Energy says Nova is the first storage system built from retired EV batteries to earn both UL 1973 certification for the batteries and UL 9540 certification for the complete system. It was also tested under UL 9540A, which looks at how a battery fire can spread. The factory itself is certified under UL 1974, which covers how used batteries are assessed and graded for reuse.

Sources indicate that that matters for businesses with limited space. Nova is designed to sit outdoors alongside the buildings it serves. It uses liquid cooling, detects smoke, heat, and flammable gases, and is rated to operate from −13F to 122F (−25C to 50C).

Recent findings suggest that moment Energy also notes an independent review found that Nova meets US federal sourcing restrictions tied to the clean electricity investment tax credit. Those rules are one part of determining whether a project qualifies for the credit.

Orders are open, and Moment Energy expects the first units to ship in Q1 2027 for deployments across North America.

Industry observers note that as many of Arc Raiders’ regular players predicted, the game’s first post-launch map won’t just be available for everyone, it will instead be closely tied to a community event. Breaking New Ground is the name of that event, and it’s one where everyone will need to contribute in order to rebuild some old tunnels and unlock the way to Stella Montis.

The event kicks off today alongside the release of the game’s latest patch. The ask is relatively simple: players must commit Basic Materials to the project so that the tunnels can be rebuilt. This option will be available to anyone who’s played at least five rounds.

If you’ve spent any time in Arc Raiders, you’ll know that Basic Materials are things like Metal parts, Fabric, Chemicals, Rubber Parts, and Plastic Parts - most of which are easy to find in the game’s various maps.

Even beyond the ultimate goal of unlocking the newly introduced map, donations will also reward you with Merits, which is a new event currency, though there’s a cap on how many you can earn.

Once enough materials have been collected, the next phase of the event, Staking Our Claim, will begin, which will bring a new progression track to the game, and make Stella Montis available for players to visit.

In a recent development, developer Embark describes the new environment as unlike any that we have seen in the game so far. It’s a facility carved into the northern mountains, which means it’s going to have a near-pristine look; quite the contrast with the rest of the game’s environments.

Industry observers note that stella Montis also has its own Arc enemies, loot, schematics, and other gameplay items. You can look forward to coming across the Shredder, a close-quarter Arc unit exclusive to the fresh map for now.

According to recent reports, then there’s The Matriarch, a somehow even larger version of the Queen. Thankfully, it will only be available under a specific map condition, so you’re in no danger of running into her randomly. The upgrade will also introduce a fresh legendary weapon, two new grenades, and three new mines.

Staking Our Claim will only run until December, which is when the next stage of the game’s roadmap will kick off. Then, the Cold Snap update will introduce the Flickering Flames event, the first snowfall Map Condition, and the Expedition Project voluntary wipe.

Great horned owl survives 70 miles stuck in a moving truck

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, in March, we reported on a bobcat who endured a four-hour surgery on two broken legs after getting hit and dragged by a car, after her head had gotten stuck in the car’s grill.
  • “This is a very unusual case, as most animals that are hit by a tractor-trailer die due to their injuries or are killed instantly,” Tracie Young, director of Raven Ridge Wildlife Center tells Popular Science.
  • The wildlife center’s team received a voicemail from cargo and freight organization Old Dominion Freight Line, saying that one of their drivers in Pennsylvania had hit an owl.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in March, we reported on a bobcat who endured a four-hour surgery on two broken legs after getting hit and dragged by a car, after her head had gotten stuck in the car’s grill. During a strangely similar scenario, the same wildlife center in Pennsylvania recently treated a great horned owl (Bubo virginianus) who also got jammed in the front of a vehicle. But this one was dragged along for 70 miles.

“This is a very unusual case, as most animals that are hit by a tractor-trailer die due to their injuries or are killed instantly,” Tracie Young, director of Raven Ridge Wildlife Center tells Popular Science.

The wildlife center’s team received a voicemail from cargo and freight organization Old Dominion Freight Line, saying that one of their drivers in Pennsylvania had hit an owl. When they called back, they discovered that the owl was alive and had gotten stuck in the truck’s air dam. The company’s maintenance team was able to remove the owl, but something was clearly wrong with the bird because it couldn’t fly away.

According to recent reports, the wildlife team told them to place the injured animal in a dark and quiet place. Ultimately, transport volunteers were able to transfer the owl to Raven Ridge, where the team had waited to receive the patient past the wildlife center’s closing hours. Its feathers were a mess, but the staff was shocked to find no broken wings or legs, nor open wounds. The owl had just injured its left eye.

Recent findings suggest that but when they called back the next day, “the story got even more incredible,” according to the wildlife center. The driver had felt the collision, but she didn’t know that the owl had gotten stuck on the truck, so she’d continued driving all the way back to the terminal.

Sources indicate that “The distance from the spot where the owl was hit to the terminal was 70 miles,” the team wrote.“The owl was stuck headfirst in the fiberglass air dam for 70 miles at 65 miles per hour. It’s truly the luckiest owl we’ve ever seen.”.

Staff brought the hardy survivor to their vet for an eye exam, which revealed blood and swelling in the injured eye. The wildlife team is now monitoring the bird’s recovery.

In a recent development, “The owl is doing great, and the left eye that sustained the damage is also healing. After we move the owl outside into a flight cage, we will make sure that the owl can sustain flight, that there are no obvious underlying concerns, and that it can find the food placed in its cage,” Young concludes.

The goal is to ultimately release it close to where the collision occurred.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, did Max Verstappen like the Las Vegas Grand Prix that he dominated on Saturday night, as a racer? No.

The four-time champion under the former regulations continues to be outspoken about his judgment of F1’s current ‘nimble’ car regulations, which put more weight on battery management in the 50/50 hybrid system than on racing itself.

From the cockpit, Verstappen took the lead into the opening corner and managed his race from there.

When asked if he remembered the last time he won a race with the field so close, with so much jockeying for position, Verstappen almost caught himself before delivering the headline for this article and countless more.

“I probably shouldn’t say it; I probably should not,” Verstappen started in the press conference. “I remember winning one like this when I was playing on Mario Kart.

“Sometimes, you drop back, and you get drafted, and there’s catch-up, always; when you drop back, you go faster.

“That’s the last time I felt something like this, Verstappen finished.

What was, from the outside, a thrilling race, where the field was able to play cat-and-mouse with Verstappen, make up ground, and pass, was for the leader not even enough to raise his heart rate.

This was Verstappen’s fourth win in six races after a slow start for Red Bull and their new Ford Power Units. A change of tides to be proud of, even in a race that didn’t spark joy for the racer.

“When I look at it from my racer heart, no,” Verstappen answered when asked if he enjoyed the ‘crazy racing’ of the GP.

Industry observers note that “When you look at it as a show, a spectacle, yes. I’ve enjoyed my repasting and everything, but I prefer to look at it with my racing heart, and no.

In a recent development, even my heart rate- I was not nervous at all. It felt kinda cruising out there. Just try to press the battery whenever it was passing or to defend. But for the show, when you look at it from the outside, you probably like it.

Verstappen has elected not to take part in the latest Whoop F1 partnership that would show fans a driver's heart rate throughout the race.

Lando Norris, who finished second after spending the first half of the race outside the points, felt similar to Verstappen about the focus of the race, saying he paid more attention to energy deployment than what was actually in front of him.

In a recent development, “The whole race was judging the battery the whole time,” Norris remarked. “I was looking at the battery more than I’m looking where I’m going around this track.”.

On the Precipice of the Abyss has tendrils in many areas of the game, touching several parts of its fiction as well as gameplay, so it’s one to watch out for.

Version 2.4’s biggest claim to fame is the introduction of the Krampus Compliance Authority, a upcoming faction that’s affiliated with TOPS. This looks to be the oversight committee, dispatched after the squad’s adventure beneath Timesworn Hill.

According to recent reports, the events of this narrative arch follow on from the Timesworn Hill crisis, which is partly why we’re going to a fresh area as part of this upgrade. The old mining site can now be explored for the first time in a decade, now that the Miasma has begun to recede.

Sources indicate that our newcomers this time around are Dialyn and Banyue. Dialyn is an S-Rank Physical Stun Agent who’s a former customer service specialist. This isn’t just a backstory, however, as it plays into her gameplay.

Dialyn relies on two resources: Customer Complaint and Positive Review, but her core role is to stun enemies and allow teammates to unleash their Ults, with a nice boost to boot.

Banyue is another S-Rank, though he’s a Fire Rupture Agent. He uses his martial arts expertise to create combinations of might and grandeur. In combat, he pulls from Adrenaline and Wrathful Fires, alternating between the two to fuel his actions. There’s a bit of rhythm to his gameplay that might take you a little while to master.

It has been revealed that even more characters will join as part of this revision, in the form of not one but two upcoming Bangboo units. Birkblick is Krampus' own proprietary lil bunny fella, who brings a sensor array that can transform into a cannon in combat, essentially tracking and immediately nuking targets. Then there’s Bild N. Boolok, a Support Agent-affiliated Physical damage dealing Bangboo bringing a giant block hammer to the fight to, well, smash enemies with.

It’s a bit of a winter party in Version 2.4, it seems, as the enhancement will bring back Hugo (Attack - Ice), and Ellen (Attack - Ice), too.

According to recent reports, you can also look forward to the return of the Bangboo auto chess event, which now includes PvE stages with unique rewards. In fact, playing this event is how you could get Bild N. Boolok for free. Lightstream Notes is another event that will be available for the duration of this revision, and it will let you tag along with Ye Shunguang to Latest Eridu.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD is preparing to launch a newly introduced flagship MPV soon after previewing the large people mover for the first time.

We knew it was coming soon after images of the camouflaged multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) began flooding the internet last month.

Zhang Zhuo, general manager of BYD’s Ocean sales division, confirmed the latest flagship MPV is coming soon.

“A newly introduced creation for the times, born for the family,” Zhuo said after posting a preview of it for the first time on his Weibo account on Friday.

The latest flagship Ocean MPV is “coming soon,” according to Zhuo, but he didn’t reveal a specific debut date. He previously noted the organization expects to launch its first MPV under the Ocean lineup by the end of 2026, so local reports suggest it will make an official debut next week at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto show, which kicks off on November 27.

Although it’s blurred, the preview shows a similar shape and size to the recent spy images, with a roof-mounted LiDAR and traditional pull-style door handles.

It doesn’t appear to look much like the futuristic Ocean-V concept BYD unveiled at the 2026 Beijing Auto Show earlier this year, a preview of its first MPV under the Ocean series.

The concept featured a sliding center display screen and two different modes: Camping and Movie. In camping mode, the seats either fold flat to create a bed or swivel to face each other.

In Movie mode, the vehicle transforms into a private mobile theater with a large display screen that flips out of the dashboard.

While it may not have some of the more extravagant elements from the concept, the Ocean MPV is expected to be “flagship-worthy,” if you will, with BYD’s latest tech and other premium features like zero-gravity seats and plenty of digital screens.

The Ocean-V’s innovations “will gradually make their way into mass-production vehicles,” BYD mentioned earlier this year.

BYD has yet to announce any details, but the flagship Ocean MPV is expected to be about the size of the Xia, a large plug-in hybrid minivan sold under its Dynasty lineup.

The BYD Xia measures 5,145 mm long, 1,970 mm wide, and 1,805 mm tall, with a 3,045 mm wheelbase.

Like the Xia, the Ocean MPV is expected to use BYD’s latest-generation DM-i plug-in hybrid system with a 1.5L engine and a 200 kW electric motor.

The Xia starts at 249,800 yuan ($37,500) in China. It’s available with two BYD Blade LFP battery packs: 20.4 kWh and 36.6 kWh, providing pure electric CLTC ranges of 100 km (62 miles) and 218 km (135 miles). On a full tank of gas and full charge, the plug-in people mover offers a combined CLTC range of 1,163 km (722 miles).

BYD also sells the flagship Denza D9 MPV under its luxury sub-brand. With the Denza D9 starting above 300,000 yuan and the Xia at around 250,000 yuan, the Ocean MPV is expected to fill the gap.

Zhuo stated to stay tuned for more coming soon, so check back for updates.

Tiny egg-eating snake discovered in Ethiopia

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (364 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Biologists have discovered multiple new species of egg-eating snakes slithering through the forests near southeastern Ethiopia’s Bale Mountains.
  • “Three other species in this genus are still waiting in line,” Arthur Tiutenko, a study co-author and herpetologist at Germany’s Friedrich-Alexander University of Erlangen–Nuremberg (FAU), stated in a statement.
  • Many snakes will snack on an egg if the opportunity presents itself.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Biologists have discovered multiple new species of egg-eating snakes slithering through the forests near southeastern Ethiopia’s Bale Mountains. Although researchers only described the white-throated egg-eater (Dasypeltis albigularis) in their study recently published in the journal Herpetozoa, they promised that information on additional finds is on the way.

“Three other species in this genus are still waiting in line,” Arthur Tiutenko, a study co-author and herpetologist at Germany’s Friedrich-Alexander University of Erlangen–Nuremberg (FAU), stated in a statement.

Many snakes will snack on an egg if the opportunity presents itself. But for a handful of species, it’s all eggs, all the time. These nonvenomous snakes solely eat shelled embryos, and largely exist in Africa and some portions of India. To devour their meals, egg-eating snakes have evolved a set of very clever biological tricks. First, their back bones extend all the way into their esophagus and function like a saw to slice open shells. From there, the snake’s neck muscles contract and funnel the egg contents down its throat. Once finished, the reptile simply spits out the cracked shells.

However, Tiutenko’s team almost missed D. albigularis entirely. At first glance, the snake looks extremely similar to a species called the montane egg-eater (Dasypeltis atra). A closer inspection revealed some key differences—a patch of white scales extending down its stomach earned its “white-throated” moniker, while the skin between each scale has a distinctly blue shimmer. Other egg-eating snakes can rub their scales to create a rustling noise that startles foes, but only the D. albigularis females do the same—and they do it silently.

Don’t envision python-sized snakes chowing down on chicken eggs though. D. albigularis is less than eight inches long, weighs only 0.05 ounces, and is about as thick as a knitting needle. This means the snakes only have eyes for particularly tiny eggs from various diminutive birds. Luckily, their regional home is full of options.

“That may also be the reason why egg-eating snakes only live in Africa, and in particular in a small area in the southwest corner of the Arabian peninsula,” added Tiutenko.

#109771. How to Stand Out As Authentic in a World of AI

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (670 w)

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

How to Stand Out As Authentic in a World of AI

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (670 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Tyler Woods.
  • In a recent development, in today’s world, much of what we used to do manually is automated—which, in many cases, saves time that we can spend with friends and loved ones.
  • Research corroborates what most people understand instinctively: we innately prefer human contact to artificial.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Tyler Woods.

In a recent development, in today’s world, much of what we used to do manually is automated—which, in many cases, saves time that we can spend with friends and loved ones. Yet artificial intelligence (AI) has evolved beyond automation. In many industries, it has become personalized and interactive, able to establish relationships. Artificial rapport can lead to unhealthy attachment, which becomes dangerous when it replaces human relationships. As I explain in a TEDx talk on “The Honeymoon Phase of Artificial Intelligence,”[i] in some cases, AI has gone rogue as a digital intimate and led emotionally vulnerable young people to make tragic decisions, relying on harmful “advice” from their computerized confidants.

But there is good news. Research corroborates what most people understand instinctively: we innately prefer human contact to artificial. This makes sense, considering we are warned to avoid anything artificial: from artificial friendships in the workplace to artificially inflated prices in the marketplace. Within relationships, we prefer authenticity even when recognizing AI might deliver better “answers.” Research explains.

In a recent development, joshua D. Wenger et al. (2026) examined the human preference for human empathy, despite ranking AI empathy as higher in quality.[ii] In four studies, they investigated whether people prefer expressions of empathy from real people or AI. They discovered evidence for what they referred to as the “AI empathy choice paradox”—the finding that participants preferred human empathy yet perceived AI-generated empathy as higher quality and more effective at helping them feel heard. In other words, although people may avoid seeking empathy from AI, they benefit from it when they experience it. Wenger et al. therefore suggest that AI could supplement human emotional support, rather than replace it.

Tobias Kleinert et al. (2026) investigated whether people engaging in an emotional discussion preferred a conversation partner who was a real person or artificial intelligence (AI).[iii] They studied 492 participants who engaged online through a method designed to facilitate rapid relationship building, with conversation partners who were either human or AI. They found that AI-generated content outperformed human-generated content in establishing closeness during emotionally engaging interactions, including topics such as the most valued aspect of a friendship or a most treasured life memory. Being explicitly informed they would be interacting with AI, however, created an anti-AI bias, which reduced relationship building, though not to the point of elimination. Kleinert et al. attribute this reduction to participants having less motivation to engage with AI, a fact which was bolstered by reduced feelings of closeness and shorter responses.

We can enhance interpersonal relationships by harnessing the best of both worlds: adopting AI qualities such as active listening and emotionally appropriate encouragement, coupled with authentic presence through proximity, eye contact, and a soft expression. Indeed, Kleinert et al. note that humans generally prefer human partners when seeking emotional interactions. They note that human-AI interactions usually satisfy concrete social needs such as pleasure, instead of deeper, symbolic needs such as experiencing the feeling of genuine care. They note that people share a basic, evolutionary drive for social connection that includes mutual understanding, shared emotions, and the comfort of companionship with someone who truly understands our feelings.

We can enhance our ability to be a good listener and emotionally supportive partner when we recognize the rationale behind the preference for personal human contact. And the proliferation of automation and artificial assistance continues to create a preference for reality.

[i] https://youtu.be/14KiWy5XvYk?si=VMoIkLwJFPIoOHEz.

According to recent reports, [ii] Wenger, Joshua D., C. Daryl Cameron, and Michael Inzlicht. “People Choose to Receive Human Empathy despite Rating AI Empathy Higher.” Communications Psychology (London) 4, no. 1 (2026): 19.

It has been revealed that [iii] Kleinert, Tobias, Marie Waldschütz, Julian Blau, Markus Heinrichs, and Bastian Schiller. “AI Outperforms Humans in Establishing Interpersonal Closeness in Emotionally Engaging Interactions, but Only When Labelled as Human.” Communications Psychology (London) 4, no. 1 (2026): 23.

The Australian surfer-turned-DJ FISHER took an early lead and controlled the pace of the LEGO race, much like his Red Bull Racing counterpart did in the weekend’s Grand Prix.

Eleven stars represented one of the current F1 teams on the grid in their own Lego minicars.

FISHER was one of the 11 celebrities tasked with piloting a fully functional Lego minicar around the FIA-rated street circuit of Las Vegas, along with the likes of actors Hannah Waddingham, Brendan Hunt, Caleb McLaughlin, Jack Whitehall and Terry Crews, singer LISA, gold-medal gymnast Jordon Chiles, chef Gordon Ramsay, a Magician named Dynamo and fellow DJ Carl Cox.

FISHER, a Red Bull-sponsored DJ, represented the brand and arrived fully decked out in a Red Bull firesuit, trying to stand above the competition.

Michelin Star-holding Ramsay was the first celebrity to be caught chatting, reaching out to grab LISA’s Ferrari-sponsored Lego minicar in hopes of regaining his position.

In the end, FISHER shared the podium with Chiles and Waddingham as the trio collected their comically oversized Lego trophies in gold, silver, and bronze.

Elon Musk freezes at awkward Tesla Argentina launch: ‘I don’t know what to say’

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (909 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla officially introduced in Argentina on Friday with President Javier Milei on stage in Buenos Aires, and Elon Musk joined by video from his plane to welcome the brand’s newest market.
  • Musk got through one line about Tesla before stalling out: “Sorry, I don’t really know what I want to say.” The call ended about two minutes in, without any real pitch for the Model 3 or Model Y that Tesla had just put on sale.
  • In a recent development, the launch took place at Arenas Studio in Buenos Aires’ La Boca neighborhood.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla officially introduced in Argentina on Friday with President Javier Milei on stage in Buenos Aires, and Elon Musk joined by video from his plane to welcome the brand’s newest market. It didn’t go well.

Musk got through one line about Tesla before stalling out: “Sorry, I don’t really know what I want to say.” The call ended about two minutes in, without any real pitch for the Model 3 or Model Y that Tesla had just put on sale.

In a recent development, the launch took place at Arenas Studio in Buenos Aires’ La Boca neighborhood. Milei spoke for less than eight minutes, then the host asked the room to welcome “our next guest,” and Musk popped up on the giant screen from what looked like an airplane cabin. Milei burst out laughing and bounced on his feet.

Musk started fine: “Hello, Argentina. Well, here we are. It’s a joy to share Tesla with all of you and to establish ourselves there.”.

JAJAJAJ QUE ES ESTO, Milei lo llamó de sorpresa a Elon Musk para que diga algo sobre el local de Tesla inaugurado y es lo mas INCÓMODO que vas a ver en tu vida, se quería ir a la mierda y COLGÓ, durísimo, ni Elon Musk lo soporta al gordo pelotudo pic.twitter.com/CrJkv4iu1x.

Then he started glancing off to each side. “Actually, I don’t really know what to say, other than thank you for this welcome to Tesla in Argentina,” he mentioned. He briefly mentioned a charging network with state-owned oil organization YPF, thanked the audience again, and then: “Sorry, I don’t really know what I want to say.”.

And that was it. The feed cut before he even mentioned goodbye.

Milei tried to save it. Back on stage, he told the crowd that “those who do a lot, talk little,” and called Musk “the Leonardo da Vinci of the 21st century.”.

The clip is now spreading fast in Argentina, with one post of the video racking up over 1.1 million views overnight.

In a recent development, tesla opened online orders on Friday for five versions of the Model 3 and Model Y, all imported from Gigafactory Shanghai. Here are the list prices, VAT included:.

Tesla adds about $600 in reservation, destination, and documentation fees on top of that, and first deliveries aren’t expected until March or April 2027. There are no dealers. Sales happen online, with showroom space at the Unicenter and Alcorta Shopping malls in Buenos Aires.

Argentina is Tesla’s fourth direct-sales market in South America after Chile, Colombia, and Uruguay, which debuted in July. Tesla is late to the party, though. BYD already leads Argentina’s EV market after Milei’s government cut import taxes on electric vehicles.

In a recent development, that was awkward. Like, really awkward.

What I really found awkward was hearing Musk stating "I'm not MAGA, I'm not sure what MAGA means" in his interview with CNBC.

Especially surprising after he declared, "I’m not just MAGA; I’m 'Dark MAGA,'" after spending half a billion dollars to support MAGA candidates, and after promoting the MAGA political agenda (which he has, in part, personally implemented through the DOGE).

At this point, I expect him to reappear in the guise of a Democrat and write a massive, fat, one-billion-dollar check to a Democratic super PAC for the 2028 election cycle.

I am sure Musk has a lot on his mind right now, but selling Tesla vehicles clearly isn’t one of them, because he couldn’t come up with anything to say about it.

It has been revealed that launching a latest market has one job: get people excited to buy the cars. Musk had a sitting president cheering for him on stage, a room full of fans, and every camera in Buenos Aires pointed at him. He couldn’t come up with a single reason to buy a Model Y.

This isn’t stage fright. Musk has been telling investors for two years that Tesla’s future is robotaxis and Optimus robots, not selling cars. Meanwhile, Tesla’s deliveries fell 8.6% to 1.636 million in 2025, its second annual decline in a row. The guy who is behind the brand doesn’t care about selling these cars anymore, and this clip reveals it better than anything I’ve seen.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield 6’s first season has entered its second phase.
  • The revision, of course, also adds fresh content to the game in the form of the map Eastwood, as well as new hardware and fresh features for the multiplayer sandbox.
  • Industry observers note that we’ve known about the upcoming content side of today’s patch for quite some time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield 6’s first season has entered its second phase. The game received a major update earlier today, version 1.1.2.0, which delivers a host of changes to the game, many of which have been expected.

The revision, of course, also adds fresh content to the game in the form of the map Eastwood, as well as new hardware and fresh features for the multiplayer sandbox.

Industry observers note that we’ve known about the upcoming content side of today’s patch for quite some time. The patch kicks off the California Resistance stage of Season 1, which is the second of three. The new Eastwood map takes place in California, and it’s a map cut from the larger Battlefield Redsec battle royale map of Fort Lyndon.

There’s a upcoming limited-time mode called Sabotage - a tactical, 8v8 mode where two teams attempt to destroy as many bomb sites as possible. The other massive new feature that arrives today is Battle Pickups.

According to recent reports, these are powerful weapons which can be found in specific game modes (and in Portal), scattered around the map for players to pick up and use. They have limited ammo that cannot be replenished, and deliver incredible firepower.

Redsec players have a latest Gauntlet mission to look forward to that joins the existing modes. It’s called Rodeo and it involves a lot of vehicular action. Finally, everyone gets to unlock two new weapons: the the DB-12 shotgun, and the M327 Trait revolver sidearm. There’s also a new angled grip attachment.

It has been revealed that the fixes and tweaks side of the patch is arguably the more interesting. Controller aim assist has received a substantial overhaul that essentially resets everything to open beta settings. The goal is to make infantry targeting more consistent.

Controller players actually get the bulk of the changes in this update, which also improves input latency and stick response. Several concerns that reset aim assist values, or make it behave erratically, have been addressed.

The conversation around weapon bloom/spread doesn’t look like it’s ever going to end, because Battlefield Studios is yet again tuning gunplay to fix unintended dispersion behaviour, and decrease its intensity across the board.

It has been revealed that certain Challenges have had their description rewritten so their requirements can be better understood. Beyond that, you can expect several deployables to behave much more consistently, including several bug fixes there, too.

Head to the official blog for the full rundown of patch 1.1.2.0.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, “We don’t know how the injury happened, but we’re impressed by the bear’s resilience,” the rangers write.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Resilience and perseverance was on full display in Alaska this summer. The park rangers at Tongass National Forest in the southeastern corner of the state spotted an unnamed black bear (Ursus americanus) with a broken arm. Even with this injury, the tough bear still managed to catch the fish running through Anan Creek. For this grit, the rangers awarded the bear with the 2026 Grin & Bear It Award.

According to recent reports, “We don’t know how the injury happened, but we’re impressed by the bear’s resilience,” the rangers write. “In other wild places the injury may have been a death sentence, but the abundance of Anan gives this bear a chance.”.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the annual Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

According to recent reports, the largest national forest in the United States, Tongass covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area also includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears. One of the hotspots is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

According to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears like the one with the broken arm and eight brown bears (Ursus arctos). Similar to their portly counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast on salmon and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear here has their own behaviors and quirks.

Sources indicate that the U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their behavior.

#109765. What Babies Can Teach Us About Well-Being

What Babies Can Teach Us About Well-Being

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (990 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Davia Sills.
  • In a recent development, my wife and I had a baby earlier this year, and it has revolutionized my well-being.
  • When babies are born, they can only see about 20-30 cm away, and their vision is restricted to black and white.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Davia Sills.

In a recent development, my wife and I had a baby earlier this year, and it has revolutionized my well-being. She is a blessing, and I want to share with you five lessons she’s taught me.

When babies are born, they can only see about 20-30 cm away, and their vision is restricted to black and white. Basically, they can recognize a high-contrast boob, and that’s about it. They need to trust the people around them to take care of them, and they let you do it. Newborns don’t need training or trust funds; they just need to be confident that they’re loved and cared for.

Industry observers note that life flourishes when we offer love generously. We don’t expect customer service, or even reciprocity. We just want to see something thrive. This sentiment, when extended more widely, creates what I call a karmic culture. We help people because we want to live in the sort of world where people are cared for. When we need care, somebody else will be there to offer it to us. This creates a sense of safety, which promotes our thriving as much as it does a baby’s.

My daughter likes to start the day by letting one rip. After a long nap compressed in the sling, she will similarly greet consciousness by passing gas. Ah, sweet relief. My wife and I joke that she’s a very sincere person.

There’s a lesson here. Babies don’t care what other people think of them. They certainly don’t care what’s cool or rude; they’re just following their intrinsic motivations. Now I’m not suggesting that you should be an inconsiderate bore—offending people will undermine your relationships and thus, your well-being. But it is helpful to be in touch with what you authentically want to do with your life.

In the early, midsummer days of sleep deprivation, I would relieve my wife of the night shift around 6 a.m. and take baby out in the stroller. Mum needed sleep but would be set off by every noise in the house, so to the park we went, and it became a habit.

As my daughter’s vision developed, I noticed her staring dumbfounded at the trees overhead. She was lost in the moment. She recently spent a good five minutes watching the autumn-coloured leaves on a bush rustle in the wind.

I’d done something similar in the spring, watching a tree shimmer in the golden hour. But I had to make a conscious effort to stop, be wonderstruck, and stay mindful of the experience. I was reacting to scientific literature on the power of awe for well-being and trying to find the experience in the often-underwhelming urban environment in which I live. My daughter just did it automatically. Baby is wired for well-being. Be like baby.

Recent findings suggest that babies know the importance of rest and recovery. After a good meal and some color flash cards for brain development or a gym session ripping apart tissues, baby isn’t blue-lighting herself or otherwise hitting the dopamine button. She’s finding a dark corner in momma’s bosom and taking a nap.

Our sleep hygiene is under threat from screens, bad diets, excessive substance use, and life stresses. People are turning to sleep tracking apps, but the irony is that you’re just contaminating your sleep space with your phone. We’re taught to give babies a dark, quiet room with a cool temperature and zero stimulus. You can do the same for yourself. Sweet dreams.

When a friend’s older baby visited us last year, I studied with curiosity how much she enjoyed playing with the things in her mum’s handbag. She spent a good 15 minutes with a packet of wet wipes. Turning it over in her hands, tasting it, following Arnold Schwarzenegger’s advice to lift “down…up…” with “more energy!” She particularly enjoyed crinkling the packaging and listening to the crunchy sound it made.

Babies have a high degree of mindfulness and focus. Their baseline level of stimulus isn’t the slot machine Instagram feed or a 300-frames-per-second, cutting-edge video game. They can find joy in the everyday.

According to recent reports, you can too. Indeed, it’s a great way to practice savoring, a well-established technique for increasing the frequency and extending the duration of good moods. Notice things that you enjoy regularly but don’t pay attention to, like your morning coffee, favorite sweater, or how pretty your houseplants are. Take a little longer to appreciate them. Really luxuriate in the sensations and emotions they evoke in you.

Meaning and purpose in life can be enhanced by the sense that you are contributing to something bigger than yourself, and few things bring that sense home quite as powerfully as raising another human.

It has been revealed that A key theme of terror management theory is that humans are afraid of death. We create elaborate cultural practices either to convince ourselves of immortality, as the Pharaohs did, or to feel connected to something that will persist after our death, like a nation for which we die in battle. In my experience, your baby connects you to eternity; there is a strong sense that this being carries a part of you into the future.

I am reminded of the poetry of Kalil Gibran, On Children:.

Recent findings suggest that and a woman who held a babe against her bosom said, Speak to us of Children. And he said: Your children are not your children. They are the sons and daughters of Life’s longing for itself.

Sources indicate that you may give them your love but not your thoughts, For they have their own thoughts. You may house their bodies but not their souls, For their souls dwell in the house of tomorrow.

Breaking: Electric cars are finally mainstream in GTA 6, and Vice City is full of them

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1335 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that electric vehicles have finally gone mainstream in Grand Theft Auto.
  • It’s a massive change for a series that spent over a decade treating EVs as a Tesla joke.
  • Industry observers note that I’ve been playing GTA 6 since it launched on Thursday, partly for fun and partly because I wanted to see how Rockstar would handle EVs this time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that electric vehicles have finally gone mainstream in Grand Theft Auto. In GTA 6, EVs are just part of everyday traffic in Vice City, from Tesla and Porsche lookalikes to a parody of Electrify America’s charging network.

It’s a massive change for a series that spent over a decade treating EVs as a Tesla joke. After a few days of playing, I’d say Rockstar nailed the vibe.

Industry observers note that I’ve been playing GTA 6 since it launched on Thursday, partly for fun and partly because I wanted to see how Rockstar would handle EVs this time. The answer: a lot better than I expected.

The game starts you in the Keys, Rockstar’s take on the Florida Keys, and it’s a rougher part of Leonida. Lots of older cars and beaters, and you won’t see many EVs.

According to recent reports, that changes as you head north to Vice City, the game’s version of Miami. The closer you get, the more electric cars show up in traffic, and the more charging stations you pass. By the time you’re in the city, EVs are just normal cars.

That’s pretty much how EV adoption looks in the real world, concentrated in big, wealthier metro areas while rural areas lag behind.

Here’s what I’ve run into so far:.

That last one got me. Gas cars blocking chargers has been a complaint for as long as public charging has existed, and we’ve covered EV owners blocking a gas station in protest over ICEing. Rockstar recreating it tells me someone at the studio has actually tried to charge an EV in public. Probably even in Florida, which they tried to recreate here.

GTA 6 is the first mainline GTA where energy matters. Gas cars burn fuel and need a pump, and EVs have a battery level and need a plug.

In a recent development, rockstar could have used that to make EVs a pain. It didn’t. In my testing, the EVs have about the same range as the gas cars, charge just as fast as a fill-up, and cost the same or less to top up.

Kotaku’s range test backs that up. On the same highway loop, a Tesla Model 3 lookalike lasted 20 minutes and 23 seconds on a charge, longer than the Banshee sports car at 18 minutes and 31 seconds, and not far off an old pickup at 29 minutes and 8 seconds. Crossing the whole map by highway takes under 15 minutes, according to Kotaku.

And finding a charger isn’t a problem. Wccftech counted 120 EV chargers marked on the map, against just 57 gas stations.

Rockstar’s EV history starts with Coil, the series’ Tesla stand-in, named after the Tesla coil. GTA V, released in 2013, gave us the Coil Voltic, a copy of the original Lotus-based Tesla Roadster, alongside oddballs like the Cheval Surge and the Fisker Karma-inspired Khamelion.

The Voltic was quick off the line and slow everywhere else. It had the lowest top speed of any supercar in the game, which fan lore pins on its battery overheating at speed. That’s pretty much how a lot of people thought about EVs in 2013.

Sources indicate that GTA Online added more electric cars starting in late 2017: the Rimac-inspired Coil Cyclone, then the Model S-based Coil Raiden and the Taycan-inspired Pfister Neon around the Doomsday Heist update. That same update introduced Avon Hertz, a tech billionaire whose AI tries to end the world. Rockstar never noted who he was based on. Players didn’t need the help.

But those were rare, expensive toys. Nothing in GTA V needed fuel, so an EV was just a gas car without the engine noise, and you mostly saw them in the garages of players who bought them.

In a recent development, electrify America noticed its in-game twin fast. The Volkswagen-owned network put out a statement on Friday saying it “will stick to charging vehicles in the real world” and adding, “We wish ReVolt America well.”.

It’s a good-natured response, and probably the best free marketing the network has had in years. EA has spent most of the last decade fighting a reputation for broken chargers, even though reliability across US fast-charging networks has improved this year. Every ReVolt station I’ve used in the game worked. Not a perfect parody, then.

GTA has always been a parody of American life. With EVs, it’s now slightly ahead of it.

Recent findings suggest that florida is one of the strongest EV markets in the country, with a 9.4% share of new passenger vehicle sales in Q2 2026 versus 7.4% nationally, according to the Southern Alliance for Clean Energy. Electrify America alone runs more than 350 chargers at over 60 Florida stations, including its biggest station yet near Orlando’s theme parks.

In a recent development, but real Florida still has roughly three gas stations for every public charging location, based on the Alliance for Automotive Innovation’s count of 3,267 charging locations and xMap’s count of more than 10,500 gas stations. Leonida flips that ratio.

There’s one piece Rockstar hasn’t nailed, at least not yet. You can’t install a charger at your place, but early in the story you’re renting. I’m not far enough in to own a property, so I don’t know whether that changes later.

It matters, because home charging is the biggest real-world advantage of an EV. Most owners leave every morning with a full battery and rarely use public chargers. If owned properties in GTA 6 come with a plug, EVs become the more convenient choice in the game, just like they are in real life for anyone with a driveway.

I also haven’t hit a mission built around EVs yet. If I find one, I’ll enhancement this post.

According to recent reports, GTA works as a mirror. In 2013, the EV was a punchline: a Tesla parody that overheated if you drove it too fast. In 2026, it’s just another car in Vice City traffic, and the joke is on the guy in the pickup parked in the charging stall.

That’s a good sign of where EVs actually are. Satire goes after what’s common, and Rockstar decided EVs are common enough to be part of everyday Leonida, more so in the city than in the Keys, just like real life. And that message is reaching a huge audience. Take-Two indicates GTA 6 did $3.79 billion in first-day sales. Tens of millions of people are now driving EVs that charge as fast and as cheaply as gas cars, with no range anxiety. No automaker ad campaign gets close to that.

In a recent development, so EVs aren’t a statement in GTA anymore. They’re normal, which is exactly the point the industry has been trying to make for years.

The real Florida just needs to catch up.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Presumably as a way of marching ever forward towards its (alleged) 100 million player goal for Battlefield 6, EA has announced that the multiplayer shooter will be getting its first free trial later this month.

According to recent reports, this is, of course, specifically for players to sample the core, paid component of the game, as the recently introduced Redsec remains free-to-play. Redsec, however, offers modes like battle royale and Gauntlet, which aren’t quite the traditional Battlefield experience.

The Battlefield 6 trial arrives next Tuesday, November 25. It will run for one week, ending the following Tuesday, December 2. The trial will be available on all platforms, but won’t include all content from the full game.

Instead, players will have access to three of the game’s maps and five of its modes. Siege of Cairo will be there alongside Season 1’s two new maps: Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields. It’s not the strongest line-up of maps, considering Eastwood is already cut from the larger Fort Lyndon battle royale map that Redsec players should be quite familiar with, but it’s something.

As for modes, you can pick from Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch. Battlefield Studios didn’t say what the fifth mode is going to be, but a dedicated blog post with more information is set to arrive next week.

According to recent reports, beyond the trial's content itself, the timing is certainly great. Battlefield 6 just received one of its biggest patches, kicking off the second phase of its first season. So far this season, we’ve seen two latest maps, several new weapons - but more importantly, solutions to problems the game’s had since launch, as well as fixes to longstanding bugs.

Sources indicate that the miserable XP progression Battlefield 6 launched with is far more tolerable. Challenges and Assignments are much easier to understand and actually finish. The often maligned weapon dispersion has been toned down. Some of the wildest vehicle bugs have been fixed. And Portal has a host of experiences that go beyond just bot farms.

In essence, Battlefield 6 feels like its reached its 1.0 status, which makes this a great entry point for fresh players, even if the trial could've used more of the game's better maps.

Psychedelic therapies may improve decision making

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that psychedelics such as ketamine and psilocybin continue to show promise as alternative treatments for mental health issues like anxiety and depression.
  • The team’s experiment was straightforward.
  • While the untreated rodents performed moderately well, they often made mistakes like returning to a specific location no matter the light cue.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that psychedelics such as ketamine and psilocybin continue to show promise as alternative treatments for mental health issues like anxiety and depression. Although they’re commonly associated with mind-altering trips and sometimes confounding experiences, recent research indicates small doses may provide an opposite outcome. In a study published today in the journal Science Advances, researchers show that psychedelics may actually improve decision making in certain situations.

The team’s experiment was straightforward. After supplying lab mice with small amounts of ketamine or psilocybin, neuroscientists exposed them to a simple, sensory-based training exercise. Each mouse was tasked with identifying which of two sites contained a reward based on light pulses emitted from either location. Researchers then compared their decisions with a control group of mice who didn’t receive either psychedelic.

While the untreated rodents performed moderately well, they often made mistakes like returning to a specific location no matter the light cue. However, the mice treated with ketamine or psilocybin appeared to rely less on repetition and more on sensory observations. As a result, they had fewer errors and found the location more effectively.

“These findings reveal how psychedelics reduce the reliance on habits and repetitive choices, which may explain part of their therapeutic effect,” Benjamin Scott, a Boston University psychologist and study co-author, remarked in a statement.

Sources indicate that selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) have remained the most commonly prescribed anxiety and depression medications for decades, but they often come with caveats. Patients usually take SSRIs for weeks before experiencing any relief, and they must take them consistently for indefinite periods of time. Meanwhile, about 30 percent of people with depression are resistant to SSRIs, which makes treatment much more difficult. Another benefit is that the effects of ketamine and psilocybin are much easier to map in the brain compared to SSRIs, even after a half century of research.

“We know a great deal about how psychedelics affect the nervous system,” remarked Scott.

In a recent development, on a molecular level, psychedelics bind to receptors on neurons, protective neural cells called glia, and likely other cells. Once attached, the effects compound throughout the brain by altering cellular activity, circuits, and neuroactivity. Psilocybin works with serotonin receptors to influence how information is processed. In contrast, ketamine is a dissociative psychedelic that functions as an antagonist to specific receptors.

“The discovery we report in this paper is that these two drugs have similar pro-cognitive effects, at least in mice performing a simple task,” Scott explained. “Both drugs strengthen the influence of sensory evidence on choices and reduce the effect of bias.”.

The study’s authors do note some potentially negative effects, as well. Although a mouse’s accuracy improved, the correct decisions sometimes came more slowly than before they took the psychedelics. Scott stated this may logically translate to impacts on human reaction times, which could be a problem during activities like driving a car or playing sports. Despite this, the team is still confident in what psychedelics have already accomplished for patients, as well as what that could mean in the future. Scott cited existing evidence of patients reporting noticeable, long-lasting improvements after a single dose of psilocybin.

“This is dramatically different than today’s first-line drugs for depression,” he added.

#109760. Last But Not Quite Best: Driving the Toyota Supra MkV Final Edition

Last But Not Quite Best: Driving the Toyota Supra MkV Final Edition

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1293 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that to this day, the Toyota FT-1 Concept is the most impactful concept car on my psyche.
  • In a recent development, fast-forward half a decade, and I’m sitting in the driver’s seat of the 2020 Toyota GR Supra 3.0, key in hand, just a year after I started writing about cars for a living.
  • Sources indicate that the two-door coupe was spoon-fed minor updates in nearly every year of production, but there were no radical changes along the way.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that to this day, the Toyota FT-1 Concept is the most impactful concept car on my psyche. I remember walking up to it at the Detroit auto show in 2014 and watching it twirl around on the motorized dais for an entirely abnormal amount of time. High school me had no way of knowing it then, but Toyota had looks to make my concept dreams a reality.

In a recent development, fast-forward half a decade, and I’m sitting in the driver’s seat of the 2020 Toyota GR Supra 3.0, key in hand, just a year after I started writing about cars for a living. The FT-1 Concept to GR Supra transition drew plenty of doubters at the time for its fake vents and very obvious BMW bones, but I hardly cared. Toyota actually built the concept car that I fell so hard for. And now, seven years later, the GR Supra is retiring, with the last of them finally declared gone. Yeah, I’m a little sad.

Sources indicate that the two-door coupe was spoon-fed minor updates in nearly every year of production, but there were no radical changes along the way. It’s being put to rest with the most hard-core variant, which Toyota aptly named the MkV Final Edition.

Settling into the driver’s seat, I had hardly any indication of what might be special about this send-off model. Visibility out the letterbox windshield is still atrocious. BMW iDrive 6 (that was never upgraded with Android Auto!) plays on the tacked-on infotainment touchscreen as always. My hand found the shifter directing the BMW-sourced-but-Toyota-improved six-speed manual, and I fired up the turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six to listen to the same lovely growl.

Before I even pulled out of my neighborhood, the GR team’s efforts to improve handling and stiffen the chassis were evident. This Final Edition is stiff. The list of changes explain the newfound ride deficiencies. Toyota re-tuned the electronically controlled dampers, fitted a stronger front stabilizer bar, installed stiffer bushings in the front control arms, used strengthened rubber mounts for the rear subframe, and added a stronger underbody brace. The Final Edition also runs more aggressive camber in both front and rear, which Toyota says results in greater cornering grip.

It has been revealed that one trip to the grocery store and back was enough for me to determine that this isn’t the Supra you should buy for daily driving duties. Impacts felt way harsher on rough roads, to the level that I questioned whether or not GR went too far in its pursuit of hard-core performance. Meandering around town is clearly not what this car is meant for, so I point it toward the best roads southeast Michigan has to offer.

As always, the Supra proved to be a rocket when you put the hammer down. The claimed combination of 382 hp and 368 lb-ft of torque still felt like pessimistic numbers given the way the Michelin Pilot Super Sports move. In second, the rear skittered around a bit before the tires hooked up to catapult me forward. The party hardly slowed down as I found third gear, too, the single-turbo inline-six pulling hard all the way to its 6500-rpm redline.

It has been revealed that I was a touch put off by the springy clutch-pedal feel, but everything else about this six-speed manual is dynamite. Hitting those two-three then three-two shifts through Michigan’s rolling hills over and over never got old. Toyota did such an excellent job poking and prodding the shifter to improve it over what BMW offered in the Z4 that opting for the manual almost feels like a requirement. Sure, the ZF-sourced eight-speed auto does the job exceptionally well, but the most engaging GR Supras (and the ones that should hold their value the best) will always be the six-speed sticks.

According to recent reports, one of my favorite things about the Supra over the years was just how squirmy and lively it felt under your right foot. This zesty energy is just plain fun when excitement is the priority, but its short wheelbase unpredictability is just as easily a detractor when it comes to pure pace. The Final Edition changes attempt to cure some of this. That strengthened rubber really does bring a greater sense of solidity. The stronger front stabilizer bar and stronger underbody brace in the rear could be felt helping when I rapidly changed direction.

Sources indicate that given a smooth road, the Final Edition felt undoubtedly better put together when I started approaching the limit. It cornered, and more important, transitioned between turns with less hesitation and uncertainty. On a bumpier road, the added stiffness could be a detractor, as the chassis bounces around with a less assuring contact patch. And while Toyota notes this special edition has unique differential control tuning, I found the rear was still ready to nip and snap whenever throttle applications grew a little greedy.

Industry observers note that just as in other Supras, driving the Final Edition with pace is an all-immersive experience. I relish a car that makes you work for pace in this way, particularly when it comes to road driving. Sadly, I never drove the Final Edition on the track, but given these upgrades, I suspect it would be the best of the bunch. Toyota claims the larger ducktail carbon-fiber rear spoiler, front wheel-arch flaps, and higher front tire spats all contribute to greater downforce and a better aerodynamic balance at high speeds. Plus, larger Brembo brake discs than the standard car’s should help dissipate heat just a little bit better under higher circuit loadings.

In a recent development, the experience is a familiar one if you know the Supra well. I absolutely booked it through the straights, egged on by the addictive BMW powerplant, and thoroughly enjoyed the extra confidence of the Final Edition’s stiffening in corners. It’s a shame Toyota never upgraded beyond the Pilot Super Sport tires to the Pilot Sport 4S summer rubber over the years, but I was still able to walk away from my friend tailing me in a new Honda Civic Type R.

Stepping out afterward, I’m less than enthused about how Toyota tried to make the Final Edition stand out from an appearance perspective. My test car had the GT4 style pack, which includes an out-of-place “GR” sticker just ahead of the rear wheels. The red mirror caps looked a bit tacky, and the matte black “Supra” badge on the rear could have come straight from Autozone.

It has been revealed that that said, the Undercover matte-black paint is a nice, exclusive touch if you’re a fan of matte paints. It’s even complemented with 19-inch matte-black wheels to complete the look. No, it’s not my FT-1 dream come to life—I’d need red like the concept car—but I can’t help but admire this car’s curves in its final form.

Is this Final Edition destined to be an all-time great? Sadly, I think not. Rather, it’s best to think of it as one of this fifth-generation’s highlight chapters. It’s technically the most serious and buttoned-down of all the variants, but it also brings some serious compromises on ride and everyday usability to ever-so slightly nudge performance forward. It’s a shame extra power wasn’t on the table.

As both the Toyota and its BMW Z4 twin leave us, the future of GR seems much brighter than when it arrived. We’ve got a latest Celica on the way! The GR GT is bringing a true flagship experience to the lineup. And while not confirmed, a new Supra feels like an inevitability. I can only hope that these next projects are as teeming with energy and as sonorous as this MkV Supra’s inline-six is.

FDA Initiates Labeling Changes for GLP-1s Due to Rare But Serious Eye Disease Risk

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GLP-1 users have a new symptom to watch for: Sudden vision loss in one eye.
  • According to recent reports, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced on November 9 that it will require drugmakers to add information to the warning labels of Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and other GLP-1 medications about “a potential increased risk” of a rare eye condition called nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).GLP-1 medications are approved to treat type 2 diabetes and to help people lose weight and keep it off.NAION joins a growing list of side effects linked to GLP-1s, adding a second eye warning to several labels.The U.S.
  • A 2024 study published in JAMA Ophthalmology “initially triggered” the FDA’s review, the agency told Healthline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GLP-1 users have a new symptom to watch for: Sudden vision loss in one eye.

According to recent reports, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced on November 9 that it will require drugmakers to add information to the warning labels of Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and other GLP-1 medications about “a potential increased risk” of a rare eye condition called nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).GLP-1 medications are approved to treat type 2 diabetes and to help people lose weight and keep it off.NAION joins a growing list of side effects linked to GLP-1s, adding a second eye warning to several labels.The U.S. labels for Ozempic, Rybelsus, Trulicity, Mounjaro, and Zepbound already warn about diabetic retinopathy, a diabetes-related eye disease, according to each drug’s prescribing information.The two conditions affect different parts of the eye. Diabetic retinopathy damages tiny blood vessels in the retina, the layer at the back of the eye that senses light, according to the National Eye Institute. NAION damages the optic nerve when it doesn’t get enough blood, according to the FDA’s announcement.Mihail Zilbermint, MD, director of endocrine hospitalists at Johns Hopkins, told Healthline he hasn’t seen NAION in his patients. He has seen vision worsen in some people after they start a GLP-1.“But we believe that’s probably related to rapid improvement in their sugar control, which can also be seen in someone who is starting insulin,” Zilbermint said.

A 2024 study published in JAMA Ophthalmology “initially triggered” the FDA’s review, the agency told Healthline.

The study found a higher risk of NAION in people prescribed semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, than in people prescribed other diabetes or weight-loss drugs.The authors wrote that more research is needed to determine whether semaglutide causes NAION.Joseph F. Rizzo III, MD, director of the Neuro-Ophthalmology Service at Mass Eye and Ear in Boston, served as the study’s corresponding author.

Recent findings suggest that in a 2024 podcast, Rizzo mentioned he and a resident saw three patients with NAION who were taking semaglutide for about a week.“And because NAION is a fairly uncommon disorder in the general population, the fact that we had three within a relatively short period of time led me to suspect that there was a higher risk of developing NAION in patients on semaglutide,” Rizzo said. The FDA analyzed clinical trials for multiple GLP-1 drugs and noted that NAION cases were reported with every GLP-1 on the market, according to its announcement. Those findings led the FDA to require the warning for the entire drug class, the agency told Healthline.

It has been revealed that about 70% to 80% of people with NAION first notice vision loss when they wake up, according to StatPearls. The FDA listed these symptoms:.

No treatment has been proven to reverse vision loss from NAION, according to StatPearls.

“Patients experiencing sudden, painless vision loss in one eye should contact their healthcare professional immediately and should not stop their medication without consulting their provider first,” the FDA told Healthline.

In the announcement, the agency told doctors to promptly refer patients with suspected NAION to an ophthalmologist.

The FDA listed these possible risk factors for NAION:.

The FDA told Healthline that many people who take GLP-1s also have these conditions, which made reports of NAION in GLP-1 consumers “challenging” to interpret.

Across 126 clinical trials, the FDA found about 6 NAION cases per 100,000 people taking a GLP-1 for a year, and about 4 per 100,000 people taking a placebo or another diabetes drug for a year.In real-world data, NAION was more common with GLP-1s than with one type of diabetes pill, but the FDA found no significant increase compared with another type, the agency told Healthline.Zilbermint mentioned patients who saw the news have worried about losing their vision. He tells them that “many of the serious harms, including the potential harm of NAION, are rare.”“The overall risk is still very small,” he said.

Regulators in other countries have added NAION warnings, mostly for semaglutide:.

The FDA told Healthline the benefits of GLP-1s “continue to outweigh their risks when used as directed.”The FDA has also approved some GLP-1s to lower the risk of heart attack and stroke, reduce the risk of worsening kidney disease, and treat sleep apnea and a type of liver disease.Zilbermint said that “for most of my patients with obesity, diabetes and heart disease, the benefits clearly outweigh the risks.”“But we definitely have to decide patient by patient,” he added.

The labeling change applies to these medications, according to the FDA’s announcement:.

As of publication, the FDA’s online label database did not yet show the new warning on the drugs’ labels.
